external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie
external_entities.notes: MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts. No trust-zone placement is stated.

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment-status webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.
external_entities.notes: No further details about the processor's environment are stated.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service through which shoppers browse and place orders and which receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: It uses email/password and session-cookie authentication for shoppers; MFA is not rolled out. It is the only component exposed to the internet.

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker that processes orders, reads and writes the orders database, and writes completed-order receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)
data_stores.notes: The order service uses a single application account with full read/write access.

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_stores.notes: Each receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: A shopper browses the storefront through the storefront API.
data_flows.notes: No transport or encryption mechanism is stated.

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: A shopper submits an order through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order
data_flows.notes: Shopper authentication uses email and password and a session cookie; MFA has not been rolled out.

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC
data_flows.notes: The gRPC call has no authentication; the order service accepts anything that can reach it.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four values in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The application account's password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for each completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket
data_flows.notes: The order service uses its own service account.

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor sends a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: third party
trust_boundaries.description: The control zone of the external card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because it is identified as a storefront API serving the storefront.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it the storefront API and describes shoppers browsing the storefront through it.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface because it is described as a Python worker rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the component as a Python worker reached over gRPC.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database has confidential data classification because it contains shopper addresses and card-last-four values in addition to orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that shopper addresses and card-last-four values live in orders-db.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive has confidential data classification because it stores completed-order receipts.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every completed order gets a receipt written to the archive.
